gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the FOPO S1 needs a separate video connection for each of its two screens and installs no driver. On a MacBook Air M2, or an M3 with its lid open, Apple says only one external display works, so only one of the S1's two screens can run.
standout_why: I compared four pages. The UPERFECT 'best triple screen laptop extenders' guide, which ChatGPT cited, says only in general that base M1 and M2 MacBooks support one external display. It never ties that limit to a product or says which extenders have a driver to work around it. Dealectric's own triple-extender page covers the Trio 3 Pro's driver workaround for base Macs and the drivers the UPERFECT, Xebec and S788 need, but it does not include the FOPO S1. ChatGPT's answers list Mac compatibility as a concern but don't apply it to any product. I could not open the cited Best Buy INVZI listing (it timed out) or the Mobile Pixels Trio page (HTTP 429).
decides: This settles the budget pick for Mac owners. On a MacBook Air M2, or an M3 with its lid open, the FOPO S1 gives one added screen, not two, because FOPO's setup has no driver. That leaves the Trio 3 Pro, which Dealectric's page says runs its second screen on base M1/M2 Macs with Mobile Pixels' free software, as the triple option under $400 for those laptops. The S1 stays a fair budget pick for Windows laptops with two video-capable ports, and for Macs that drive two or more external displays.

findings.label: MacBook Air M2 external display limit
findings.value: One external display (up to 6K at 60 Hz)
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple names no driver or software route. Put together with FOPO's statement, only one S1 screen runs on this laptop.

findings.label: MacBook Air M3 external display limit
findings.value: One external display (up to 6K at 60 Hz) with the lid open. A second (up to 5K at 60 Hz) only with the lid closed.
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (15-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: A lid-mounted extender is used with the lid open, so the closed-lid second display doesn't help here. That last point is my reasoning, not Apple's wording.
